description:
1.5 Hour Bansuri to Unwind | Breathe and Let Go

If it's 11pm and your brain is rehearsing tomorrow's meeting — start here. Bansuri's breath-driven flute is the closest sound to your own slow breathing finally remembering itself. Let it breathe for you.

90 minutes of slow bamboo flute, tuned to a gentle low frequency designed to help the body unwind and settle into deep sleep.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Bansuri — the bamboo flute, one of the most breath-driven instruments in Indian classical music
- Long flowing notes with natural breathing pauses
- A gentle low-frequency layer that helps the body let go
- Unbroken sound — no abrupt fades, no startling moments

⏱ Chapters
0:00   Settling in
12:00  Body sinking
30:00  Drifting off
60:00  Deep sleep zone
80:00  Gentle return

🧠 How to use:
Press play. Lights low. Don't try to sleep — let the flute set the pace. Phone face down, somewhere out of reach.

⏱ Best for:
• Trouble falling asleep
• 1am to 4am wakeups
• Mind-too-loud nights
• Background for deep rest
• Evening wind-down

📺 Subscribe to Raga Focus for daily uploads:
- Sitar, Sarangi, Veena, Surbahar, Bansuri, Tanpura and other Indian instruments
- Music for anxiety, overthinking, sleep, stress, emotional release

— Raga Focus

thumbnail_prompt: Pichwai/Kangra miniature painting style, ornate gold-and-cream patterned border with subtle lotus and moon motifs, aged warm parchment background, late-evening palette (deep indigo with single warm oil lamp glow and soft moonlight). Central figure: serene woman in deep-blue-and-cream sari with gold accents seated cross-legged playing bansuri (recognizable as a long bamboo flute held horizontally to the lips) in a quiet candle-lit room. Soft moonlight through a small window. A single sleeping figure curled in a low bed nearby or a still water bowl reflecting moonlight as visual sleep-cue. Bold dark-teal serif overlay text reading 'DRIFT TO SLEEP' top-center, traditional Devanagari-influenced serif typography, high contrast for mobile readability. Aged warm cream parchment palette, contemplative restful sleep mood, single composed scene, no clutter.
suno_prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals. Warm bansuri flute solo in raga Yaman, deep evening sleep mood, smooth breath-driven melodic flow with very long sustained notes, no percussion, no tabla, 432Hz tuning, 55-65 BPM very slow tempo, sparse expressive phrases with long silences between them, mid-to-low register (warm not high-pitched), cinematic meditation production, hypnotic and grounding, suitable for extended looping in post-production, begins immediately with bansuri already playing, no fade-in, no silent intro, full sonic presence from first note. CRITICAL register notes: bansuri MID-register warm not high — high bansuri triggers alertness, opposite of sleep. Sparse phrasing, long silences. Recent ships AVD slipping suggests audio may be too dense — counteract by deliberately sparse, low-register phrasing. deeply settled, like a body finally surrendering to rest

production_spec.loop_seam: 10s in / 30s out, Suno extend 3-4x → loop in post to fill 90 min
production_spec.notes: EMOTIONAL TAG ROTATION: clip 1: 'deeply settled, like a body finally surrendering to rest' · clip 2: 'gently hopeful, like tension quietly dissolving' · clip 3: 'deeply introspective, like breath held before release' · clips 4-7 cycle. Yaman tonic D or C. CRITICAL: Bansuri MID-REGISTER warm — Suno default is often bright/high-pitched flute, which is alerting not sleep-inducing. Explicitly state 'warm low-mid register bansuri', 'sparse phrasing', 'long silences', 'breath-driven slow'. AVD WILDCARD: recent ships dropped 6-8 AVD points — verify first clip is genuinely sleepy (you should feel drowsy listening) before committing extend. Mix: Suno -3dB, Binaural -22dB (very quiet for sleep audience), Tanpura drone -24dB. 432Hz canonical, Delta 2Hz for deep sleep brainwave. LUFS -16dB (quieter than usual — sleep audience plays while falling asleep, too loud disrupts sleep onset). DIRECT REPLICA of Apr Bansuri Deep Sleep hero (24K views / 5.98% CTR — channel's #1 CTR ever).
